title: Postoperative flumazenil administration following preanesthetic anxiolysis with benzodiazepines in children
summary: Avoiding anxiety is one of the 10N quality criteria in pediatric anesthesia. In clinical practice, this often leads to the administration of anxiolytic benzodiazepines during preoperative preparation. However, one complication of this administration is an overhang into the postoperative phase. The aim of this monocentric, retrospective study is to identify risk parameters for benzodiazepine-induced carryover effects in the postoperative period in connection with drug antagonism therapy.

interventions.name: Retrospective, monocentric cohort analysis of patient records/files/anesthesia protocols with regard to dosage, route of administration, duration of administration, time of benzodiazepine administration for preoperative anxiolysis, and comparison with postoperative flumazenil needs.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients under the age of 18 who underwent surgery involving anesthesia at the Pediatric Orthopedic Clinic and who received benzodiazepines for anxiolysis prior to surgery.
Exclusion criteria:
incomplete data recording
